caption: The drawing displays a detailed architectural design for an iron cross intended to be mounted on a cemetery gate. The central focus is a large cross with ornate scrollwork at its base, incorporated into a section of a wrought iron fence. The cross features straight vertical and horizontal bars with decorative ends, and two large scrolls forming symmetrical spirals on each side below the horizontal bar. Below the cross are additional pointed iron finials atop vertical bars of the gate. On the left and right edges of the design, there are brick or stone pillars illustrated as rectangular blocks framing the gate. Measurements are given in inches, with the iron assembly shown as 70 inches wide, 40 inches between pillars, and 50 inches tall. In the upper right, text reads "IRON CROSS Surmounting CEMETERY GATE" in a mix of printed and cursive lettering. To the right of the main drawing, a smaller inset shows a perspective view of the gate positioned between two masonry pillars, with the iron cross and gate assembly mounted in place. The drawing is composed of precise, black ink linework on a beige or light tan background, typical of technical architectural plans.
title: Cross
